Subject: VPC instrumentation gating and SIEM certification

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the initial onboarding last week. We need a short validation exercise so our security/compliance team can sign off on Redwood running in our private VPC. The ask list from our side: 

- Confirm recommended forwarder topology for Splunk HEC and an alternative syslog/CEF path.
- Exact egress firewall rules (IPs, ports) and TLS/mTLS requirements for the forwarder.
- Example ingest manifest mapping (fields, timestamps, service tags) so our SIEM team can map incoming events.
- Guidance on trace hook sampling headers and how to correlate traces with logs.
- A minimal QA checklist we can use to certify successful handoff and retention policy alignment.

Can you share a runbook and a short sample manifest we can load into our staging SIEM? We're aiming to close certification by end of next week.

Appreciate it —
Lara Nguyen
Security Lead, Acme Health
security@acme-health.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Nguyen <security@acme-health.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC instrumentation gating and SIEM certification

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a focused runbook and a sample ingest manifest to get you started (see attachments). High-level plan below; I put owners and an estimated time to complete each step.

1) Forwarder topology (owner: Acme + Redwood; ~1 business day)
   - Preferred: Splunk HEC over TLS (443) using company-managed forwarder inside the VPC.
   - Alternative: Syslog/CEF to an on-prem collector if HEC not allowed; we recommend TCP with TLS and mutual auth.

2) Firewall & egress (owner: Acme infra; ~30–60 mins to open/test)
   - Allowed outbound targets: redwood-ingest-01.redwood.ai (52.33.44.12), redwood-ingest-02.redwood.ai (52.33.44.13).
   - Ports: 443 (HEC/TLS), 6514 (syslog-TLS) as fallback.
   - Protocol: HTTPS/TLS 1.2+; optional mTLS if you require client certs. We provide a short cert rotation guide in the runbook.

3) Auth & handshake (owner: Redwood; ~30 mins)
   - We support token-based HEC keys and an mTLS mode (mutual TLS). Tokens are single-use per forwarder and can be rotated.
   - If using mTLS, we will provide CA cert and client cert template; you must install in the forwarder.

4) Ingest manifest & field mapping (owner: Acme SIEM; ~2 hours)
   - Attached "siem-ingest-sample-manifest.json" shows canonical fields we expect: timestamp (RFC3339), service, host, level, trace_id, span_id, request_id, message, and optional structured payload (json).
   - Please map your parsers to these fields; we included example Splunk props/transforms in splunk-props-example.conf.

5) Trace hooks & correlation (owner: Redwood + Acme devs; ~1 day)
   - We recommend propagating trace headers: X-Request-Id, traceparent (W3C), and x-redwood-trace (Redwood's short-id).
   - Sampling: enable 1% at ingress for high-volume services and increase to 10% for onboarding QA. Our runbook has a small script to stitch trace IDs into logs and verify presence in the manifest.

6) Certification checklist (owner: Acme Security; <1 day)
   - Load test events to STAGING SIEM, confirm all canonical fields present, verify TLS and auth mode, validate retention window (we support configurable retention on your dedicated instance), run the correlation smoke test for traces + logs.

Next steps:
- I've attached vpc-obsv-runbook-v1.pdf and the sample manifest.
- Can we schedule a 45-minute handoff call tomorrow at 11:00 AM PT to walk the SIEM team through the manifest? If not, propose alternatives and we'll adjust.

I'll be on the call with Kimberly (forwarder) and Marcus (trace hooks).

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick technical notes from the forwarder perspective (pulled from the runbook):

- Splunk HEC specifics: we recommend HEC batch size = 500 events, timeout = 10s. HEC token-per-forwarder avoids cross-tenant mixing. If you use HEC over non-443 ports, ensure NAT preserves source IP for geo-IP tags.

- Syslog/Cef fallback: prefer TCP/TLS (RFC 5425) to avoid UDP drops. For high-throughput services push directly to forwarder; for constrained networks prefer buffered forwarder inside the VPC and ship over TLS.

- MTU/fragmentation: we saw issues when VPC MTU < 1500 + gzip payloads; set forwarder chunking to 1MB or lower.

- Timestamp fidelity: ensure your agent timestamps are RFC3339 with timezone. If not available, include event_received_time for ordering.

I'll prepare a short splunk-props-example.conf to match the manifest and attach it to the thread. Also note: if you require CEF, our parsing uses CEF extensions to map trace_id -> extension field 'rt'.

-kim

Thanks — one practical addendum before the call: we've created a small trace-header adapter that runs as a sidecar in the forwarder pod. It normalizes incoming headers (traceparent -> trace_id, x-redwood-trace -> short_id) and injects trace_id into the json payload if missing. I attached trace-adapter-config.patch.

If you prefer not to run a sidecar, we can also provide a lightweight function (python) that runs on the forwarder and does the same mapping; let me know which you prefer and we'll include it in the runbook v1.1.

Also attached: splunk-props-example.conf (mapping rules) and a one-page controls summary PDF.

-Marcus
